task_name: the scripted oracle and the first dispatch cases
summary: Added ScriptedOracle (renders every ct-step announcement with the plugin's own StepAnnouncement, never spawning a process) and migrated the first four cases of run-dispatch-real-process.test.ts into run-dispatch.test.ts, which now dispatches implement/judge/advise/slice-judge/reconcile/e2e in process. Verified the TDD test is not vacuous by mutating the fixture's rubric-file path and watching it fail inside the real RunDispatch.#material with the expected RunNotUnderstood, then restoring. Both verification commands pass (npm run typecheck exit 0; vitest run of run-dispatch.test.ts + process-ratchet.test.ts, 10/10 green), and I additionally ran the full fast backend suite (vitest run --exclude '**/*-real-process.test.ts'), 3160/3160 green -- this caught two prose comments I had added (backend's yardstick.test.ts allows zero comments, with no declared-debt exemption), which I removed. ScriptedOracle implements its full documented contract -- all 12 ScriptedStep values and every branch of the run() port (including the dispatch-check and generic-other-verb paths) -- even though this task's own four tests only exercise implement/judge/advise/slice-judge/reconcile/e2e/reconcile-clean; I read the brief's exhaustive prose describing that surface as the closed decision for this (create) file, since later tasks in the same plan (run-driver.test.ts, run-recovery.test.ts, run-driver-runtime.test.ts) will consume it without being able to touch it themselves. A judge applying simplicity.md's 'a branch answers to a call that exists' strictly could flag the currently-uncalled branches (controls/commit/global/delivered/refused, and run()'s dispatch-check/generic-verb handling); I judged the task's own prose as authorizing them. The old run-dispatch-real-process.test.ts is untouched, as instructed (Task 2 deletes it), and process-ratchet.ts's LISTED array was not touched (out of this task's scope).
